claim: NaV1.7 has been identified as a potential novel analgesic target due to its involvement in human pain syndromes.
source: The voltage-gated sodium (NaV) channel NaV1.7 has been identified as a potential novel analgesic target due to its involvement in human pain syndromes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Clinically available NaV channel-blocking drugs are not selective among the nine NaV channel subtypes, NaV1.1–NaV1.9.
source: However, clinically available NaV channel-blocking drugs are not selective among the nine NaV channel subtypes, NaV1.1–NaV1.9.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of current drugs.

claim: GDC-0310 engages the NaV1.7-VSD4 through an unexpected binding mode orthogonal to the arylsulfonamide inhibitor class binding pose.
source: Here, we report that GDC-0310 engages the NaV1.7-VSD4 through an unexpected binding mode orthogonal to the arylsulfonamide inhibitor class binding pose, which identifies a previously unknown ligand binding site in NaV channels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by cryo-EM structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GDC-0310 binding identifies a previously unknown ligand binding site in NaV channels.
source: Here, we report that GDC-0310 engages the NaV1.7-VSD4 through an unexpected binding mode orthogonal to the arylsulfonamide inhibitor class binding pose, which identifies a previously unknown ligand binding site in NaV channels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM structure of GDC-0310 bound to VSD4.

claim: The GDC-0310 binding mode enabled the design of a novel hybrid inhibitor series that bridges the aryl- and acylsulfonamide binding pockets.
source: This finding enabled the design of a novel hybrid inhibitor series that bridges the aryl- and acylsulfonamide binding pockets and allows for the generation of molecules with substantially differentiated structures and properties.
evidence: This is supported by the design, synthesis, and structural characterization of hybrid compounds presented in the manuscript.

claim: NaV channels contain 24-transmembrane segments linked in four homologous domains (DI-DIV).
source: NaV channels contain 24-transmembrane segments linked in four homologous domains (DI-DIV), where four peripheral voltage-sensor domains (VSD1-4) surround a central ion-conducting pore module that houses the ion selectivity filter and key ligand and toxin binding sites.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about NaV channels.

claim: Four peripheral voltage-sensor domains (VSD1-4) surround a central ion-conducting pore module in NaV channels.
source: NaV channels contain 24-transmembrane segments linked in four homologous domains (DI-DIV), where four peripheral voltage-sensor domains (VSD1-4) surround a central ion-conducting pore module that houses the ion selectivity filter and key ligand and toxin binding sites.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about NaV channels.

claim: All clinically available NaV channel inhibitors lack significant molecular selectivity among the NaV1.1–1.9 subtypes owing to the high sequence conservation found at the ligand binding site within the central cavity of the ion-conducting pore module.
source: Traditionally, all clinically available NaV channel inhibitors lack significant molecular selectivity among the NaV1.1–1.9 subtypes owing to the high sequence conservation found at the ligand binding site within the central cavity of the ion-conducting pore module (McKerrall and Sutherlin, 2018; de Lera Ruiz and Kraus, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: PF-04856264 bound to an unprecedented receptor site in VSD4 with demonstrated molecular selectivity for human NaV1.7 over other subtypes.
source: A breakthrough study in 2013 by McCormack and colleagues reported the discovery of an arylsulfonamide antagonist, PF-04856264, that bound to an unprecedented receptor site in VSD4 with demonstrated molecular selectivity for human NaV1.7 over other subtypes (McCormack et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to McCormack et al., 2013.

claim: PF-05089771 did not meet clinical endpoints in human subjects with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy, possibly due to poor target coverage and the intolerable doses required to achieve efficacy.
source: However, the related development candidate PF-05089771 did not meet clinical endpoints in human subjects with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy, possibly due to poor target coverage and the intolerable doses required to achieve efficacy (Swain et al., 2017; McDonnell et al., 2018; Siebenga et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trial reports.

claim: GDC-0276 was halted in phase I clinical trials due to safety concerns and potential off-target effects likely attributed to the high lipophilicity of the compound.
source: Additionally, an alternate acylsulfonamide inhibitor that also targeted the VSD4 receptor site in NaV1.7, GDC-0276, was halted in phase I clinical trials due to safety concerns and potential off-target effects likely attributed to the high lipophilicity of the compound (Rothenberg et al., 2019; Safina et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trial reports and includes speculative reasoning about the cause.

claim: The GX-936 arylsulfonamide inhibitor binding mode revealed that the anionic sulfonamide group engages the fourth arginine gating charge (R4) to trap VSD4 in an activated conformation.
source: Using an engineered human VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVAb bacterial channel chimera and X-ray crystallography, the binding mode of the GX-936 arylsulfonamide inhibitor revealed that the anionic sulfonamide group engages the fourth arginine gating charge (R4) to trap VSD4 in an activated conformation, which in turn stabilizes a non-conductive, inactivated state of the channel (Ahuja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ahuja et al., 2015 crystal structure.

claim: The GX-936 binding mode stabilizes a non-conductive, inactivated state of the channel.
source: Using an engineered human VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVAb bacterial channel chimera and X-ray crystallography, the binding mode of the GX-936 arylsulfonamide inhibitor revealed that the anionic sulfonamide group engages the fourth arginine gating charge (R4) to trap VSD4 in an activated conformation, which in turn stabilizes a non-conductive, inactivated state of the channel (Ahuja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ahuja et al., 2015 crystal structure.

claim: Molecular docking studies presumed that the acylsulfonamide inhibitors also bound VSD4 in an analogous manner to arylsulfonamides, despite points of inexplicable SAR.
source: This shortcoming led molecular docking studies to presume that the acylsulfonamide inhibitors also bound VSD4 in an analogous manner, despite points of inexplicable SAR (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sun et al., 2019 and describes prior assumptions.

claim: The VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimera displays the expected domain-swapped arrangement with numerous densities assigned as phospholipids bound to the channel.
source: The VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimera displays the expected domain-swapped arrangement with numerous densities assigned as phospholipids bound to the channel, confirming the maintenance of a native membrane-like environment (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 1.

claim: The ion-conducting pore module of the VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimeric channel is closed, consistent with a nonconductive or inactivated state.
source: As seen in previous NaVPas structures (Clairfeuille, 2019; Shen et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2018), the ion-conducting pore module of the VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimeric channel is closed, consistent with a nonconductive or inactivated state.
evidence: This is supported by comparison to previous structures cited and the current structure.

claim: 111 water molecules were assigned for the highest resolution structure.
source: The quality and resolution of our structure allowed us to assign 111 water molecules for the highest resolution structure (Figure 1E, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by the structural data shown in Figure 1E and Video 1.

claim: The 2.9 Å resolution cryo-EM map revealed that the S1-S2 and S3-S4 helices from VSD4 form a clamshell-like structure that closes over GNE-3565.
source: The 2.9 Å resolution cryo-EM map revealed that the S1-S2 and S3-S4 helices from VSD4 form a clamshell-like structure that closes over GNE-3565 (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1A), similar to the binding pose reported for GX-936 (Ahuja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 2.

claim: The ionized arylsulfonamide group of GNE-3565 (measured pKa = 5.8) bisects VSD4 to salt-bridge directly to R4 on the S4 helix.
source: Specifically, the ionized arylsulfonamide group of GNE-3565 (measured pKa = 5.8) bisects VSD4 to salt-bridge directly to R4 on the S4 helix, while the central phenyl ring extends perpendicular between the S2 and S3 helices to directly contact established subtype-selectivity determinants Tyr1537 and Trp1538 on the S2 helix (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure and measured pKa value.

claim: The central phenyl ring of GNE-3565 extends perpendicular between the S2 and S3 helices to directly contact established subtype-selectivity determinants Tyr1537 and Trp1538 on the S2 helix.
source: Specifically, the ionized arylsulfonamide group of GNE-3565 (measured pKa = 5.8) bisects VSD4 to salt-bridge directly to R4 on the S4 helix, while the central phenyl ring extends perpendicular between the S2 and S3 helices to directly contact established subtype-selectivity determinants Tyr1537 and Trp1538 on the S2 helix (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 2.

claim: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) between the GNE-3565-VSD4 and the GX-936-VSD4 structures is 0.667 (714–714 atoms).
source: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) between the GNE-3565-VSD4 and the GX-936-VSD4 structures (Ahuja et al., 2015) is 0.667 (714–714 atoms) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), supporting long-held assumptions by medicinal chemistry teams that all structurally related arylsulfonamides should be expected to complex to VSD4 through similar determinants (Swain et al., 2017; Weiss et al., 2017; Graceffa et al., 2017; McKerrall et al., 2019; Roecker et al., 2021; Focken et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the two structures.

claim: A cryo-EM structure of GDC-0310 complexed with VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVPas channel was determined to 2.5 Å resolution.
source: To investigate the binding pose of a representative NaV1.7-selective acylsulfonamide, GDC-0310 (Figure 3A) was complexed with the VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVPas channel in nanodiscs and a cryo-EM structure was determined to 2.5 Å resolution (Figure 3B–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is a primary structural result reported in the manuscript.

claim: The binding mode of GDC-0310 revealed an unexpected and previously unknown pocket that formed between the S3 and S4 helices.
source: Remarkably, the binding mode of GDC-0310 revealed an unexpected and previously unknown pocket that formed between the S3 and S4 helices (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3.

claim: The aryl and acyl moieties of GDC-0310 and GNE-3565 bind in the same region, but the remainder of the acyl receptor site is orthogonal to the corresponding binding domain reported for the aryl class.
source: While the aryl and acyl moieties of GDC-0310 and GNE-3565 bind in the same region, the remainder of the acyl receptor site is orthogonal to the corresponding binding domain reported for the aryl class (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: The anionic acylsulfonamide of GDC-0310 participates in salt-bridge bonding interactions with R4 and R3 through the carbonyl and sulfonamide oxygen atoms, respectively.
source: In detail, the anionic acylsulfonamide of GDC-0310 participates in salt-bridge bonding interactions with R4 and R3 through the carbonyl and sulfonamide oxygen atoms, respectively (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The aryl ring of GDC-0310 splits the S3 and S4 helices to occupy a lipophilic pocket, displacing the S3 helix laterally by ~3 Å relative to the GNE-3565-VSD4 structure.
source: Moreover, the aryl ring of the GDC-0310 splits the S3 and S4 helices to occupy a lipophilic pocket, displacing the S3 helix laterally by ~3 Å relative to the GNE-3565-VSD4 structure (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: The cyclopropyl substituent of GDC-0310 makes effective van der Waals interactions with I1574 and I1588 from S3 and I1601 and I1604 on S4.
source: It is notable that the cyclopropyl substituent of GDC-0310 makes effective van der Waals interactions with I1574 and I1588 from S3 and I1601 and I1604 on S4 (Figure 3G), while the alpha-methylbenzylamine 'tail' region sits almost entirely within the lipid bilayer (Figure 3A and C), where density for this portion of the inhibitor is only poorly resolved (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The alpha-methylbenzylamine 'tail' region of GDC-0310 sits almost entirely within the lipid bilayer.
source: It is notable that the cyclopropyl substituent of GDC-0310 makes effective van der Waals interactions with I1574 and I1588 from S3 and I1601 and I1604 on S4 (Figure 3G), while the alpha-methylbenzylamine 'tail' region sits almost entirely within the lipid bilayer (Figure 3A and C), where density for this portion of the inhibitor is only poorly resolved (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure and poor density for this region.

claim: The relative depth of the GDC-0310 binding site in relation to the membrane-water interface is approximately 8 Å.
source: Considering the relative depth of the­ GDC-0310 binding site in relation to the membrane-water interface (~8 Å), our structure suggests a membrane access pathway for acylsulfonamides to the VSD4 receptor site, which has important implications for understanding the pharmacology, SAR, and potential development liabilities of the inhibitor series (Payandeh and Volgraf, 2021).
evidence: This is a measurement from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The structure suggests a membrane access pathway for acylsulfonamides to the VSD4 receptor site.
source: Considering the relative depth of the­ GDC-0310 binding site in relation to the membrane-water interface (~8 Å), our structure suggests a membrane access pathway for acylsulfonamides to the VSD4 receptor site, which has important implications for understanding the pharmacology, SAR, and potential development liabilities of the inhibitor series (Payandeh and Volgraf, 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and cited literature.

claim: The Tyr1537 side chain on S2 exists in a down rotamer conformation and does not contact GDC-0310 directly.
source: Notably, this structure also reveals that the Tyr1537 side chain on S2 exists in a down rotamer conformation and does not contact GDC-0310 directly, which provides the first direct structural rationale for why the selectivity profiles between the acyl and arylsulfonamide classes differ substantially (Figure 3D, vide infra; Bankar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The Tyr1537 conformation provides the first direct structural rationale for why the selectivity profiles between the acyl and arylsulfonamide classes differ substantially.
source: Notably, this structure also reveals that the Tyr1537 side chain on S2 exists in a down rotamer conformation and does not contact GDC-0310 directly, which provides the first direct structural rationale for why the selectivity profiles between the acyl and arylsulfonamide classes differ substantially (Figure 3D, vide infra; Bankar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and cited literature.

claim: GNE-9296 (compound 2) retained substantial potency, affording channel blockade at an IC50 of 47 nM (n = 8).
source: Seeking to leverage existing knowledge of the arylsulfonamide binding pocket, GNE-9296 (compound 2) was synthesized in an attempt to directly graft on a significant portion of the GNE-3565 scaffold. Gratifyingly, this molecule retained substantial potency, affording channel blockade at an IC50 of 47 nM (n = 8).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A cryo-EM structure of GNE-9296 bound to the VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVPas channel confirmed that the molecule adopts the desired hybrid binding mode.
source: A cryo-EM structure of GNE-9296 bound to the VSD4 NaV1.7-NaVPas channel confirmed that the molecule adopts the desired hybrid binding mode (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The anionic group of GNE-9296 binds in the same position as in the aryl and acyl poses, interacting closely with R4.
source: Here, the anionic group of the novel hybrid compound binds in the same position as in the aryl and acyl poses, interacting closely with R4, as seen for the aryl-like binding (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Inhibitor 3 demonstrated an IC50 of 16 nM (n = 12).
source: This SAR proved translatable to the hybrid class molecules, resulting in inhibitor 3 (IC50 = 16nM, n = 12; Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GNE-1305 (compound 4) demonstrated potent NaV1.7 inhibition (IC50 = 9 nM, n = 8).
source: On this basis, we designed N-benzothiazolyl sulfonamide GNE-1305 (compound 4), which demonstrated potent NaV1.7 inhibition (IC50 = 9nM, n = 8, Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Molecule 5 shows reduced potency (IC50 = 74 nM, n = 8) compared to GNE-1305.
source: Although this molecule shows reduced potency (IC50 = 74 nM, n = 8), lack of substantial small molecule contact with the lipid bilayer is an uncommon feature in all other known NaV1.7 VSD4 domain inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Molecule 5 lacks substantial small molecule contact with the lipid bilayer, which is an uncommon feature in all other known NaV1.7 VSD4 domain inhibitors.
source: Although this molecule shows reduced potency (IC50 = 74 nM, n = 8), lack of substantial small molecule contact with the lipid bilayer is an uncommon feature in all other known NaV1.7 VSD4 domain inhibitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure and comparison to other inhibitors.

claim: High-quality cryo-EM maps of VSD4 in complex with ICA121431 have recently been reported from full-length human NaV1.3 channel protein.
source: Importantly, high-quality cryo-EM maps of VSD4 in complex with ICA121431 have recently been reported from full-length human NaV1.3 channel protein (Li et al., 2022), indicating that SBDD efforts targeting a particular NaV channel subtype would likely benefit from exploring both engineered and native channel sample options at early project stages.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: Arylsulfonamides have shown high levels of selectivity against NaV1.5, NaV1.1, and NaV1.4, but lower selectivity against NaV1.2 and NaV1.6.
source: Typically, arylsulfonamides have shown high levels of selectivity against NaV1.5, NaV1.1, and NaV1.4, but lower selectivity against NaV1.2 and NaV1.6.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about arylsulfonamide selectivity patterns.

claim: Several acylsulfonamides have been characterized with very high selectivity over NaV1.2 and NaV1.6.
source: In comparison, several acylsulfonamides have been characterized with very high selectivity over NaV1.2 and NaV1.6 (Bankar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bankar et al., 2018.

claim: Residues forming the contours of the acylsulfonamide binding pocket show high sequence homology across NaV isoforms.
source: Interestingly, residues forming the contours of the acylsulfonamide binding pocket show high sequence homology across NaV isoforms, suggesting that selectivity for this class is likely an allosteric phenomenon.
evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis that leads to a speculative conclusion.

claim: Selectivity for the acylsulfonamide class is likely an allosteric phenomenon.
source: Interestingly, residues forming the contours of the acylsulfonamide binding pocket show high sequence homology across NaV isoforms, suggesting that selectivity for this class is likely an allosteric phenomenon.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on sequence homology data.

claim: The structure of GDC-0310 provides a structural rationale for the relative slow dissociation kinetics of acylsulfonamide inhibitors compared to arylsulfonamides.
source: Our structure of GDC-0310 provides a structural rationale for the relative slow dissociation kinetics of acylsulfonamide inhibitors compared to arylsulfonamides (Bankar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and cited kinetics data.

claim: The acylsulfonamide pocket is buried more deeply into the plasma membrane than the arylsulfonamide pocket.
source: Specifically, the acylsulfonamide pocket is buried more deeply into the plasma membrane than the arylsulfonamide pocket, and may only be available through a membrane-access pathway that first involves partitioning of the molecule into the hydrophobic core of the membrane.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structures.

claim: The acylsulfonamide pocket may only be available through a membrane-access pathway that first involves partitioning of the molecule into the hydrophobic core of the membrane.
source: Specifically, the acylsulfonamide pocket is buried more deeply into the plasma membrane than the arylsulfonamide pocket, and may only be available through a membrane-access pathway that first involves partitioning of the molecule into the hydrophobic core of the membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural data.

claim: The arylsulfonamide pocket is more open to the outer membrane leaflet–aqueous interface, potentially offering access or egress directly from (or to) the solvent compartment.
source: In comparison, the arylsulfonamide pocket is more open to the outer membrane leaflet–aqueous interface, potentially offering access or egress directly from (or to) the solvent compartment.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structures with speculative implications.

claim: Slow dissociation kinetics may be associated with membrane-access pathways for small molecules binding to transmembrane proteins.
source: It is increasingly recognized that slow dissociation kinetics may be associated with membrane-access pathways for small molecules binding to transmembrane proteins (Payandeh and Volgraf, 2021; Mason et al., 1991; Coleman et al., 1996; Anderson et al., 1994; Masureel et al., 2018; Austin et al., 2003; Rhodes et al., 1992; Sykes et al., 2014; Dickson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Hybrid molecules 2–5 are selective for NaV1.7 over the cardiac channel NaV1.5.
source: Although selectivity was not a key endpoint of our proof-of-concept studies described here, hybrid molecules 2–5 are selective for NaV1.7 over the cardiac channel NaV1.5.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimeric construct had been previously shown to complex with small molecule inhibitors and peptide toxins known to target VSD4.
source: Thus, we sought to exploit an engineered human VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas cockroach channel chimeric construct that had been previously shown to complex with small molecule inhibitors and peptide toxins known to target VSD4 (Clairfeuille, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Clairfeuille, 2019.

claim: The recovered protein yields following expression and purification were 50 µg/L.
source: The recovered protein yields following expression and purification (50 µg/L) allowed us to readily pursue reconstitution of the VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas channel into lipid nanodiscs (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a measured protein yield from the expression and purification protocol.

claim: The cryo-EM data collection and processing procedures allowed routine obtainment of 3D-reconstructions in the 2.2–3.0Å resolution range around the VSD4 inhibitor binding site.
source: Small molecule inhibitors were added prior to sample vitrification, followed by cryo-EM data collection and processing procedures, which allowed us to routinely obtain 3D-reconstructions in the 2.2–3.0Å resolution range around the VSD4 inhibitor binding site (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a summary of the resolution achieved across multiple structures.

claim: The visualization of many well-resolved water molecules bound within the VSDs and coordinated within the ion selectivity filter provides new insights into the interactions that might occur during gating charge transfer and ion conduction, respectively.
source: The visualization of many well-resolved water molecules bound within the VSDs and coordinated within the ion selectivity filter provides new insights into the interactions that might occur during gating charge transfer and ion conduction, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation of water molecules.

claim: GNE-3565 is representative of an advanced series of arylsulfonamide class NaV1.7 inhibitors that demonstrates channel blockage at subnanomolar concentrations with mixed subtype selectivity.
source: Arylsulfonamide GNE-3565 is representative of an advanced series of arylsulfonamide class NaV1.7 inhibitors that demonstrates channel blockage at subnanomolar concentrations with mixed subtype selectivity (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of GNE-3565 based on prior data.

claim: The GNE-3565, arylsulfonamide VSD4 receptor binding site can be divided into three regions: an anion-binding pocket, a selectivity pocket, and a lipid-exposed pocket.
source: As for GX-936, the GNE-3565, arylsulfonamide VSD4 receptor binding site can be divided into three regions: an anion-binding pocket, a selectivity pocket, and a lipid-exposed pocket (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a classification based on the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The cryo-EM structures serve to highlight a dynamic environment in VSD4 where the S1-S4 helixes can be differentially separated by the binding of distinct small molecule inhibitors.
source: Our cryo-EM structures serve to highlight a dynamic environment in VSD4 where the S1-S4 helixes can be differentially separated by the binding of distinct small molecule inhibitors (Figure 2D and Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of multiple cryo-EM structures.

claim: Progenitor compound 1 offers reasonable potency against NaV1.7 (IC50 = 25 nM, n = 8).
source: Accordingly, re-evaluation of potency and physicochemical property data available for previously synthesized NaV1.7 inhibitors identified progenitor compound 1, which offers reasonable potency against NaV1.7 (IC50 = 25 nM, n = 8; Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and reduced molecular weight (350 g/mol) and lipophilicity (cLogP = 2.7).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Compound 1 has reduced molecular weight (350 g/mol) and lipophilicity (cLogP = 2.7) compared to GDC-0310.
source: Accordingly, re-evaluation of potency and physicochemical property data available for previously synthesized NaV1.7 inhibitors identified progenitor compound 1, which offers reasonable potency against NaV1.7 (IC50 = 25 nM, n = 8; Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and reduced molecular weight (350 g/mol) and lipophilicity (cLogP = 2.7).
evidence: These are calculated or measured physicochemical properties.

claim: GDC-0310 has a molecular weight of 543 g/mol and lipophilicity (cLogP = 5.2).
source: GDC-0310 was a relatively unattractive starting point for hybridization because of its high molecular weight (543 g/mol) and lipophilicity (cLogP = 5.2).
evidence: These are calculated or measured physicochemical properties.

claim: In the hybrid configuration of GNE-9296, Y1537 adopts a similar arrangement as observed for the arylsulfonamides.
source: Notably, in this hybrid configuration, Y1537 adopts a similar arrangement as observed for the arylsulfonamides (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The aryl ring in the S2/S3 binding pocket of GNE-9296 was shifted ~1 Å away from the VSD4 core compared to arylsulfonamides such as GNE-3565.
source: Further analysis of the cryo-EM structure of GNE-9296 revealed that the aryl ring in the S2/S3 binding pocket was shifted ~1 Å away from the VSD4 core compared to arylsulfonamides such as GNE-3565 (data not shown).
evidence: This is a measurement from comparison of cryo-EM structures.

claim: The acylsulfonamide moiety of GNE-9296 places the two aryl substituents 4.7 Å apart.
source: We hypothesized that the acylsulfonamide moiety of GNE-9296, which places the two aryl substituents 4.7 Å apart, might not be fully optimized for use in hybrid inhibitors.
evidence: This is a measurement from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: An arylsulfonamide moiety would position the two aryl substituents at a distance of ~3.3 Å.
source: In comparison, an arylsulfonamide moiety would position these two groups at a distance of ~3.3 Å.
evidence: This is a measurement or calculation based on molecular geometry.

claim: In the GNE-1305 structure, the typical face-on pi-stacking orientation of the S2/S3 substituent with Y1537 is observed while maintaining efficient space filling in the S3/S4 pocket.
source: Here, we observed the typical face-on pi-stacking orientation of the S2/S3 substituent with Y1537 while maintaining efficient space filling in the S3/S4 pocket.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure of GNE-1305.

claim: The use of an engineered VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimeric channel construct was essential to produce sufficient yields of recombinant protein capable of routinely returning multiple cryo-EM samples per preparation.
source: We further note that our use of an engineered VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas chimeric channel construct was essential to produce sufficient yields of recombinant protein capable of routinely returning multiple cryo-EM samples per preparation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the authors' experience with the system.

claim: The VSD4-NaV1.7-NaVPas system repeatedly delivered high-resolution depictions of the VSD4 inhibitor binding site and thus contrasts with prior accounts of VSD4 in cryo-EM structures of full-length human NaV1.7 channels.
source: This system repeatedly delivered high-resolution depictions of the VSD4 inhibitor binding site and thus contrasts with prior accounts of VSD4 in cryo-EM structures of full-length human NaV1.7 channels (Shen et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2022)
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work supported by citations.

claim: The co-structure of GDC-0310 was critical to contextualize historical differences between aryl- and acylsulfonamide NaV1.7 inhibitors.
source: The co-structure of GDC-0310 was critical to contextualize historical differences between aryl- and acylsulfonamide NaV1.7 inhibitors, which include divergent SAR in the linker phenyl ring and tail regions, disparate NaV family selectivity patterns, and differences in on-rates and off-rates (Safina et al., 2021; Sun et al., 2019; Bankar et al., 2018; Luo et al., 2019; DiMauro et al., 2016; Focken et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural data and cited literature.

claim: Previous efforts to model acylsulfonamide binding have attempted to dock molecules into the GX-936 co-structure and have proposed subtle changes in molecular register and/or pose to explain the non-translatable SAR.
source: Previous efforts to model acylsulfonamide binding have attempted to dock molecules into the GX-936 co-structure and have proposed subtle changes in molecular register and/or pose to explain the non-translatable SAR (Sun et al., 2019; Kotla et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior modeling studies.

claim: The molecular features of aryl- and acylsulfonamide inhibitors diverge because they occupy distinct, but overlapping, pockets within the VSD4 domain.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the molecular features of aryl- and acylsulfonamide inhibitors diverge because they occupy distinct, but overlapping, pockets within the VSD4 domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of the cryo-EM structures.

claim: Mutation of key non-conserved residues proximal to the binding pocket observed in the GX-936 co-structure has been shown to alter NaV1.7 potency consistent with selectivity patterns observed for other NaV family members.
source: Mutation of key non-conserved residues proximal to the binding pocket observed in the GX-936 co-structure has been shown to alter NaV1.7 potency consistent with selectivity patterns observed for other NaV family members (Ahuja et al., 2015; Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ahuja et al., 2015 and sequence alignment data.

claim: The disparate binding pockets for aryl and acyl inhibitor classes provide a clear rationale for their historically divergent patterns of selectivity.
source: Nonetheless, the disparate binding pockets for these two inhibitor classes provide a clear rationale for their historically divergent patterns of selectivity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data.

claim: Potent hybrid inhibitors can be designed with fewer membrane-associated elements than prior generation NaV1.7 inhibitors.
source: We have demonstrated that potent hybrid inhibitors can be designed with fewer membrane-associated elements than prior generation NaV1.7 inhibitors, and anticipate that this will offer opportunities to develop molecules with improved lipophilic ligand efficiency and/or differentiated pharmacokinetic profiles.
evidence: This is supported by the design and characterization of hybrid molecules.

claim: Hybrid inhibitors can access selectivity determinants from both the S2/S3 and S3/S4 pockets simultaneously, offering a tantalizing opportunity to develop exquisite selectivity over other NaV isoforms.
source: Hybrid inhibitors can also access selectivity determinants from both the S2/S3 and S3/S4 pockets simultaneously, offering a tantalizing opportunity to develop exquisite selectivity over other NaV isoforms.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural data.

claim: Transmembrane proteins, particularly intrinsically dynamic ones including ion channels, transporters, and GPCRs, may commonly present privileged structural motifs that are rich with opportunities for the discovery of novel druggable pockets.
source: We speculate that transmembrane proteins, particularly intrinsically dynamic ones including ion channels, transporters, and GPCRs, may commonly present privileged structural motifs that are rich with opportunities for the discovery of novel druggable pockets.
evidence: This is a speculative generalization based on the findings.

claim: A robust pipeline for high-resolution structural determination of small-molecules bound to NaV1.7-VSD4 suitable for use in iterative structure-based drug design campaigns has been developed.
source: In summary, we have developed a robust pipeline for high-resolution structural determination of small-molecules bound to NaV1.7-VSD4 suitable for use in iterative structure-based drug design campaigns.
evidence: This is a summary of the methodological achievement described in the manuscript.

claim: The first co-structure of an acylsulfonamide inhibitor bound to the VSD4 domain of NaV1.7 reveals an unexpected and unique binding mode.
source: We also report the first co-structure of an acylsulfonamide inhibitor bound to the VSD4 domain of NaV1.7, revealing an unexpected and unique binding mode.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM structure of GDC-0310.

claim: The GDC-0310 structure provides clear rationale for previously unexplainable divergence in the in vitro pharmacological behavior between inhibitor classes.
source: This finding provides clear rationale for previously unexplainable divergence in the in vitro pharmacological behavior between inhibitor classes, and inspired the development of hybrid inhibitors that engages VSD4 in a novel conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and comparison to prior pharmacological data.

claim: The findings highlight the power of cryo-EM as an enabling drug discovery technology.
source: Our findings highlight the power of cryo-EM as an enabling drug discovery technology and offer insights into ion channel structural dynamics that are potentially applicable to related targets and other target classes.
evidence: This is a general conclusion based on the work presented.

claim: NaV1.7 is expressed predominantly in the peripheral nervous system.
source: The NaV1.7 channel is expressed predominantly in the peripheral nervous system, and genetic studies have identified compelling loss-of-function and gain-of-function phenotypes in human pain syndromes, prompting significant efforts to develop NaV1.7-selective inhibitors as potential novel analgesic drugs (Dib-Hajj et al., 2013; Payandeh and Hackos, 2018; McKerrall and Sutherlin, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Genetic studies have identified compelling loss-of-function and gain-of-function phenotypes in human pain syndromes related to NaV1.7.
source: The NaV1.7 channel is expressed predominantly in the peripheral nervous system, and genetic studies have identified compelling loss-of-function and gain-of-function phenotypes in human pain syndromes, prompting significant efforts to develop NaV1.7-selective inhibitors as potential novel analgesic drugs (Dib-Hajj et al., 2013; Payandeh and Hackos, 2018; McKerrall and Sutherlin, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior genetic studies.

claim: NaV channels initiate and propagate action potentials in excitable cells and play important roles in health and disease.
source: Voltage-gated sodium (NaV) channels initiate and propagate action potentials in excitable cells and play important roles in health and disease (Catterall et al., 2005; Ahern et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.
